reasons: Classification is correct: the grant in p0002 is unqualified "revocable" and names only Customer, and p0025 affirmatively bars third-party access absent Kubient's written approval, so there is no path to add affiliates/contractors — this fails the fallback (affiliates covered on notice) and sits in walk-away territory.

The redline reaches the playbook position on all material terms: affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are added to the grant, at-will revocation is replaced with revocation only on expiration/termination under paragraph 4, and successor transferability is tied to the existing assignment right in paragraph 14(h).

The conforming edit to p0025 is necessary — without it the third-party access prohibition would nullify the new affiliate/contractor coverage — and it appropriately keeps Customer responsible for their compliance.

Edits are proportionate: commercial core of the grant (limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, no sublicense, stated purpose) is preserved; the elevated changed-character ratios reflect the required deletion of "revocable/non-transferable, non-assignable" language rather than gratuitous rewriting.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position and explains the operational rationale without lecturing.
